summary: Export of the daily GPU utilization dashboard focusing on headroom and burst scenarios. Contains per-cluster/pool utilization, short-term forecast, and flags where predicted headroom < 10%. Generated after observed traffic surge in US-West and post-rollout changes in EU-West.

conclusions: Two clusters (us-west1-cluster-b and eu-west1-cluster-c) show predicted headroom under 5% for the next 12 hours — classify as immediate risk. APAC clusters have spare capacity and can absorb non-latency-sensitive bursts. Fleet-level headroom dropped from ~18% to ~9% in the last 24h due to marketing-driven traffic and a model rollout with higher memory footprint.
action_items: Trigger INFRA-8421 runbook: increase autoscale-min on us-west1-cluster-b to 20% capacity (non-preemptible) and set aggressive scale-up threshold for 2 hours
Schedule cross-region routing for non-critical batch requests to apac-sin clusters for next 48h (update routing policy: region_priority)
Investigate model-v1.9 rollout for memory/KV cache regression (rollback to v1.8 if KV pressure persists) and correlate with PR #5123
Notify sales/finance to prepare short-term Dedicated capacity commit for Q2 (estimate additional 200 GPUs across US/EU)
Add automated alerting rule: predicted_headroom_pct < 10% -> oncall + infra-leads page
raw_notes: Notes to self: numbers pulled from Grafana CSV export (UTC). Baseline defined as median utilization over prior 7 days. Forecast uses exponential smoothing (alpha=0.35) over 6-hour sliding windows. Warning threshold = 10% headroom, Critical = 5%. Consider enabling preemptible->non-preemptible fallback during canary if we're unable to scale quickly. Follow-up: validate autoscale response time under synthetic load (INFRA-8430).
